name: rMG – Image Optimizer
author: Preston Elrod / ProxSEO

sections.description:
rMG – Image Optimizer helps WordPress sites feel faster by reducing wasted image weight without forcing you to manually resize files, replace uploads, or rebuild pages.

Your original Media Library files stay untouched. rMG prepares lighter image versions for the pages visitors actually load, then serves those optimized files when they are ready. The result is a cleaner image workflow for site owners and faster pages for visitors.

Simple controls let you choose WebP or AVIF, adjust quality, manage lazy loading, add smooth fade-in behavior, and tune sharpness. The optimized media library gives you a single place to review generated images and delete them whenever needed.

Free service provided by ProxSEO, your all-in-one partner for websites, SEO, hosting, and digital growth.

External Services

This plugin connects to the hosted ProxSEO rMG image optimization service when an administrator starts site optimization, requests page optimization, or runs queued background optimization.

The service receives the site URL, local callback REST URL, plugin version, WordPress version, site name, selected published page URLs or page IDs, viewport names, and image/page metadata needed to return optimization results. The service may request the site’s public pages and the plugin’s authenticated local callback endpoint to analyze published content.

The service endpoint defaults to https://api.proxseo.com and can be changed with the RMGIO_ENDPOINT_URL constant, environment variable, or rmgio_default_endpoint_url filter. The local callback key can be configured with the RMGIO_LOCAL_API_KEY constant or environment variable.

Service provider: ProxSEO / rMG. Terms of Service: https://proxseo.com/rmg-image-optimizer/terms-of-service/. Privacy Policy: https://proxseo.com/privacy-policy/
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to the /wp-content/plugins/rmg-image-optimizer directory, or install the plugin through the WordPress admin.
  2. Configure the rMG service endpoint for the site if you do not want to use the default ProxSEO endpoint.
  3. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress.
  4. Open the rMG admin menu to review settings and start optimization.
sections.faq:
Will rMG change my original images?

No. rMG keeps your original uploads in place and stores generated optimized images separately.

Does this replace original uploads?

No. Generated variants are stored separately, and your original Media Library files remain untouched.

Which image formats can I use?

rMG can generate WebP or AVIF optimized images. If an optimized image is not available, WordPress continues serving the original file.

Can I remove optimized images later?

Yes. Generated images can be reviewed and deleted from the optimized media library.

Does this plugin use a third-party service?

Yes. The plugin contacts the configured rMG image optimization service when optimization or queue processing runs. See the External Services section for details.
